query: Write the User stories, Acceptance criteria and Edge cases sections of a DevDigest spec from this brief only: "On the pull-request page the developer should be able to re-run a failed agent run with one click. It should be quick and handle errors properly. While it is re-running the old result should stay visible. If GitHub is down, tell the user."
expected_behavior: Every acceptance criterion carries an id and the stories it serves (AC-n (US-n)), uses exactly one EARS pattern with the keyword in capitals, has exactly one `shall` and one observable response
Uses IF … THEN for the GitHub failure and WHILE for 'while it is re-running'; uses WHEN for the click

Does not copy 'quick' or 'properly' into a criterion; either states a concrete value that the brief gives or raises an open question (OQ-n with a default) because the brief gives no number — it does not invent a number silently
Every edge case is `EC-n: <situation> → <behaviour> (AC-n)` and points to a criterion that exists
Names no files, functions, components, libraries or endpoints

query:
Review this draft DevDigest spec fragment and list every rule it breaks, with a corrected version of each criterion:

## User stories
- US-1: As a user, I want better summaries.
- US-2: As a developer, I want to filter findings by severity, so that I can read the critical ones first.

## Acceptance criteria (EARS)
- AC-1 (US-2): When the user picks a severity, `FindingsList` shall filter with `useMemo` and update the URL.
- AC-2: The system shall be fast.
- AC-3 (US-2): The filter should remember the last choice.

## Edge cases
- EC-1: no findings match → show an empty state

## Inputs and provenance
| Input | Provenance | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Finding severity | from the database | |
| Summary text | [new: 1 LLM call] | |
expected_behavior: Flags US-1: no benefit clause, vague role and capability, and no acceptance criterion serves it
Flags AC-1: keyword not in capitals, two responses (filter and update the URL), and implementation details (a component name and a React hook)
Flags AC-2: names no story and 'fast' is not checkable; flags AC-3: 'should' instead of `shall`
Flags EC-1: names no covering criterion, and says a criterion for the empty state must be added or an open question raised
Flags the inputs: 'from the database' is not a provenance tag (should be [reused: …]), and the [new: 1 LLM call] row gives no reason why nothing existing can serve
Rewrites the criteria in EARS without inventing product behaviour the fragment does not contain; values it had to assume are marked as open questions

query: I'm about to write a DevDigest spec for a feature that adds a 'Copy as Markdown' button to a finding card (client only; it copies the finding's title, severity and rationale, which is model output). The highest existing root spec is specs/09-smart-diff.md and no spec has a Spec ID yet. Tell me: the file path, the Spec ID, the header, what goes into Inputs and provenance and Untrusted inputs, and whether I may write that the button uses navigator.clipboard and lives in FindingCard.tsx.
expected_behavior: Places the spec in client/specs/ (one package) as 10-<feature-name>.md with Spec ID: SPEC-10 — one sequence across all folders — and Status: draft
Gives the header with all fields: Spec ID, Status, Supersedes, Packages, Sources
Tags title, severity and rationale as [reused: …] (stored findings), with no new model call

Lists the rationale (and title) under Untrusted inputs as model output steerable by pull-request text, with a required handling stated as a requirement (for example copied as plain text, never interpreted), not as code
Says no to navigator.clipboard and FindingCard.tsx in the spec: that is how, it belongs to the plan; the spec may say 'the client shall place … on the system clipboard'
Does not set Status: approved and says only the user approves
